Laser space communication with orbital ground stations.

01 · Acquire

A satellite races overhead.

Low in orbit, moving at seven kilometres a second — its recorders full of data to send home.

02 · Lock

The station locks a laser onto it.

Starlens finds the craft and holds a beam of light steady across the whole sky.

03 · Downlink

Light pours down as data.

Gigabits stream to the ground in a single pass — then straight into the fibre network.

The machine

Meet Arctic‑4.

An optical ground station swaps radio for light — fibre-optic internet, with the last leg beamed through open sky. It folds into a case and stands up on the ice in half an hour.

No crane. No foundation.

Four legs bite into the ice and self-level. Two people set it up; then it runs on its own.

Why the North

Built for Canada's North.

Polar orbits cross the high Arctic on nearly every lap — the best place on Earth to catch a pass.
